widgetData.content:
County can move level on points with Huddersfield Town at the top of League One this weekend, as Jimmy McNulty’s side take on promotion rivals Reading at Edgeley Park.

The Hatters currently sit second in the table following a 2-1 win against AFC Wimbledon in their last league outing a fortnight ago. Goals from Jack Diamond and Ethan Ennis saw County come from behind to beat the Dons and secure a fourth consecutive home league win.

With leaders Huddersfield not in action this weekend due to the international break, a win would see County go level on points with the Terriers – although they would require a four-goal win to replace them at the top.

County have twice been in cup action since that win against Wimbledon, confirming top spot in their Jersey Mike’s Trophy group following a penalty shootout win against Tranmere Rovers, whilst also coming from 2-0 down with ten men to beat Cray Wanderers in the Emirates FA Cup. That incredible comeback win at Flamingo Park has set up a second round tie against this weekend’s opponents, Reading.

Leam Richardson’s side are also looking to narrow the gap at the top of the table this weekend following a strong start to the league season. The Royals currently sit four points behind County in sixth place, but were beaten 2-0 in their last league game away at rivals Oxford United.

A first win at Edgeley Park since 1971 would move them above Luton Town in the table and leave them a point behind County and the automatic promotion places.

Things you need to know:

  • The last remaining tickets for this game are available to purchase in the Cheadle End and the Pop Side! Click here to get tickets online today, and join us as we look for a fifth straight league win!
  • Please note that Edgeley Park is now a cashless stadium. Please ensure you have card or contactless payment methods ready for all purchases (excluding matchday bucket collections).
  • Don’t forget to turn up early to Edgeley Park to visit the County Courtyard! Doors open from 12pm. Click here for more details.
  • Saturday’s game will be available for overseas supporters to stream on County TV - featuring live commentary from Jon Keighren and Sam Byrne. Audio commentary will also be available for supporters based in the UK. Click here to subscribe to County TV.

Our Opponents:

Reading have endured a frustrating three seasons in the third tier since their relegation from the Championship in 2023. Prior to that year, the Royals hadn’t competed at this level since 2002, but they have failed to record a top six finish or challenge consistently for promotion since returning to League One.

They came close in 2024/25, missing out on the play-off places to Leyton Orient on the final day of the campaign despite a host of off-field issues. That impressive campaign provided plenty of optimism heading into last season under new ownership.

Three straight defeats to start the league campaign was not the start their supporters would have envisaged, however, and the Royals went on to win just two of their opening 12 league games to occupy a place in the relegation zone.

A much-needed victory was then secured against Northampton Town, but a 1-1 draw at home to Doncaster Rovers in their next league game saw the club part company with manager and club favourite, Noel Hunt.

Hunt had a popular five-year stint with the club during his playing days and came close to guiding them to an unlikely play-off spot in his first few months in charge, but departed with the club sitting 19th and just two points above the bottom four.

A swift recruitment process saw former Wigan Athletic and Rotherham United boss Leam Richardson appointed as Hunt’s successor. Richardson won the League One title with the Latics during his last spell in the third tier, but arrived on the back of overseeing Rotherham’s relegation from the Championship.

Richardson went unbeaten in his first three league games in charge, picking up wins against Stevenage and Blackpool in the process.

Consecutive defeats against Peterborough United and Bradford City left them still languishing down in 18th, but a superb run over the festive period soon saw them surge into the top half of the table.

The Royals won four and drew one of five league games between mid-December and January, a run capped by a 1-0 win against County at the Select Car Leasing Stadium.

Richardson’s side were just four points off the play-off places at that stage. Although they then suffered a brief dip in form, another strong run of just one defeat in nine saw them eventually break into the top six in March following a 2-1 win at Burton Albion.

They remained in the play-off places heading into April following a 3-0 win against Richardson’s former side, Wigan, but then went on to pick up just two points from their final six games, falling away to finish in 12th – 12 points behind Stevenage in sixth.

It was still an impressive turnaround from the situation that Richardson inherited back in October, and the manager was backed heavily in the transfer market over the summer.

Colchester United’s Kyreece Lisbie and former County loanee Josh Stokes have added further quality to a front line that already boasts one of the division’s best finishers in Jack Marriott.

It’s that exciting forward line that has shone in the opening months of the season, despite the Royals failing to win their opening two league games. A 4-3 defeat at home to Luton Town on the opening day was followed by a 0-0 draw with AFC Wimbledon, but a first win was then secured with a 5-0 thrashing of Mansfield Town.

Richardson picked up the League One Manager of the Month award for September after guiding Reading to further wins against Blackpool and Notts County, as well as picking up a point away at Wycombe.

They carried that momentum into October, with three wins and just one defeat in six league games moving them into the play-off places in League One. The highlight of that run was undoubtedly a 5-1 win away at MK Dons, with Lisbie grabbing a brace for the Royals.

The club’s razor-sharp attack has been blunted somewhat in their last two league games, drawing 0-0 at Plymouth Argyle before that 2-0 loss at Oxford, but they returned to form in some style in the Emirates FA Cup last weekend, winning 5-0 at Peterborough United.

Despite having to deal with a number of absentees this weekend through a combination of injury, suspension and international duty, they arrive at Edgeley Park in a good place – knowing a win will see them make further inroads at the top of the table.

Match Stats:

  • Saturday will be the 36th competitive meeting between the two sides. County have won ten of those previous encounters to Reading’s 12.
  • County have lost just two of 18 previous home games against Reading, going unbeaten in the last 13 meetings at Edgeley Park.
  • Kyle Wootton has scored in each of his two home appearances against Reading for County.
